text:
jordan: quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime roadmap section. i had a few clarifying Qs about: 1) kernel selection during sudden load shifts, 2) recommended batching defaults for low-latency interactive endpoints vs high-throughput offline jobs, and 3) how KV cache invalidation works during model rollouts.
lin: good set. short answers: 1) kernel selection is cautious 1 we avoid mid-request kernel swaps unless there's sustained latency degradation and queue build-up, 2) interactive vs bulk batching have different defaults, 3) KV invalidation supports rollout-driven deletes + TTL. happy to expand.
jordan: "cautious" sounds hand-wavy. what metrics and thresholds trigger a switch?
lin: we evaluate a rolling 60s window. triggers: sustained p95 > target by configured delta, aggregate queue depth > threshold, and high in-flight token ratio. we also require the predicted win (estimated token-cost reduction) to exceed a small margin to avoid flip-flopping.
diego: ops nuance: we prefer to perform kernel changes at steady-state; ops-bot will only auto-suggest switches if it's per-tenant-safe. cross-tenant kernel changes require manual review.
nicole: for batching defaults: interactive default = max_batch_size 12, soft_latency 40ms; bulk default = max_batch_size 256, soft_latency 180ms. these are now in Console as heuristic presets.
jordan: can Optimize surface these per-route? it'd be helpful if the console recommended a safe delta when toggling batch size.
maya: yes. Optimize will suggest new max_batch_size and expected cost/latency tradeoffs derived from recent traces. we plan to show estimated token-cost impact and p95 delta.
jordan: cache invalidation: is it TTL-only or do we have targeted invalidation on rollout?
lin: rollout hook available. default prefix TTL is 30m, but a rollout can trigger immediate prefix invalidation for the affected model id when enabled.
diego: to avoid stampedes we use staged invalidation (canary shards first) and an optional grace-serving mode where stale entries are allowed for a short request cap while the backend warms caches.
jordan: what's the guidance for PMs drafting rollout plans?
maya: recommended checklist: 1) enable targeted prefix invalidation if model outputs are non-deterministic, 2) use canary percentage 1-5% for 5-10 minutes, 3) watch p95 & token-cost charts and have auto-rollback threshold at p95 +20% relative.
lin: added: kernel-switch runbook is at /internal/runbooks/kernel-switch.md (ops only). public doc in Console under Runtime -> Kernel & Rollouts.
jordan: awesome. i'll file a doc request to make the console guidance more step-by-step.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout for model: redwood-beta at 1870012600 by maya.
lin: acknowledging the auto-suggest for kernel switch on model: test-88 (checking logs).
jordan: thanks all, closing this thread unless more Qs.
